report.liteDisclaimer: This result was generated using the KineLab Lite browser engine. The Lite engine uses simplified analytic PK models and approximate grid/Monte Carlo inference. It does not use full ODE-based pharmacometric modelling, hierarchical Bayesian inference, or validated postmortem redistribution modelling. The output should be interpreted as scenario exploration and uncertainty visualization, not as a definitive forensic conclusion.

ethanol.widmarkDistribution: Distribution volume (Vd) treated as a single subject-level constant. KineLab computes Vd from the subject panel via Widmark r·weight when both body weight and biological sex are supplied (r ≈ 0.68 male / 0.55 female; sex-unknown spans the male–female range). When the subject panel is empty the engine falls back to a typical-adult uniform Vd of 35–70 L. A Vd override on the priors panel takes precedence over both.
ethanol.linearElimination: Elimination is linear (zero-order) in mg/L per hour throughout the modelled window. The KineLab inverse-inference engine and the priors / report / override surfaces all use mg/L/h; the forward Widmark calculator at /modeling?mode=ethanol presents the same parameter as g/dL/hour for clinical readability.

subjectPanel.helpFirstOrder: Body weight scales L/kg drug-row Vd values to litres at inference time; sex and age are persisted with the case for forensic provenance.
subjectPanel.helpZeroOrder: Body weight + sex steer the Widmark r·weight calculation for ethanol Vd (r ≈ 0.68 male / 0.55 female). Leave blank to fall back to a typical-adult uniform Vd of 35–70 L.

warnings.multipleDosesLatestOnly: Multiple dose events are not yet modelled; only the most recent dose is used.
warnings.routeApproximated: This route is approximated as immediate absorption (identical to the oral model). Route-specific bioavailability and absorption rate are not modelled.
warnings.lowEss: Low effective sample size: the importance sampler is dominated by a few high-weight draws, so the posterior intervals are unreliable. Widen the priors or increase the draw count, and treat the result as approximate.
warnings.matrixNoConversion: The measurement matrix differs from whole blood, but no matrix conversion is applied — the concentration is used as-is. Interpret the result with that in mind.
warnings.ethanolNotZeroOrder: This ethanol case is being run with a first-order model, but ethanol follows zero-order (Widmark) elimination. Check the priors — the result is unreliable.
warnings.nonethanolZeroOrder: This analyte is being run with a zero-order (ethanol/Widmark) model, which is only appropriate for ethanol. Check the priors — the result is unreliable.
warnings.parentMetaboliteApprox: This analyte's model card describes a parent/metabolite chain, but the engine runs it as a parent-only first-order approximation — the metabolite chain is not modelled. Interpret the result accordingly.
warnings.instantaneousAbsorption: Absorption is treated as instantaneous (no absorption rate), so concentrations sampled near the peak (Tmax) are not reliable. Set an absorption rate constant (ka) to use the rising-then-falling Bateman model.
warnings.matrixUnsupported: The measurement matrix is not supported by this analyte's model, and no matrix conversion is available. The inference was not run — pick a supported matrix or run the case in whole blood.
warnings.matrixMixed: The observations span more than one matrix. Cross-matrix conversion is not yet available, so the inference was not run — use a single matrix for all measurements.
warnings.inferenceFailed: The inference could not be completed for this component, so no result was produced. Check the dose, measurements, and priors.
warnings.highRejectRate: {{pct}}% of simulation draws were rejected as nonsensical. Results may be less reliable.
warnings.fewValidDraws: Very few valid simulation draws. Results are unreliable.
warnings.unstableDoseFromConcentration: Dose estimates from a single concentration may be highly unstable, especially if time since dose or route is uncertain.
warnings.backwardExtrapolation: Backward extrapolation over {{hours}} hours amplifies uncertainty substantially.
warnings.defaultWeight: Vd is in L/kg; using default 70 kg body weight. Enter actual weight for better accuracy.
warnings.oralSimplified: Oral mode uses a simplified equation that does not model absorption phase. Results near Tmax may be unreliable.
warnings.highSensitivity: Output is highly sensitive to {{parameter}} ({{pct}}% of variance).
warnings.terminalPhaseExtrapolation: The extrapolation assumes the measurement was taken in the terminal elimination phase: the curve follows the model’s terminal half-life, and absorption and distribution are not modelled.
warnings.nonlinearExtrapolation: This model has saturable (Michaelis–Menten) elimination, so the concentration does not decline first-order. Extrapolating from a single measurement is not supported for this analyte.
warnings.nonlinearDoseSolve: This model has saturable (Michaelis–Menten) elimination, so concentration is not proportional to dose. The dose cannot be back-calculated by scaling for this analyte.
warnings.doseSolveNeedsDoseTime: The dose cannot be back-calculated without an intake time and a timed measurement.
warnings.doseSolveNeedsPositiveConcentration: The measured concentration must be greater than zero to back-calculate a dose.
warnings.doseSolveZeroPrediction: The model predicts zero concentration at the measurement time, so no dose can explain the measurement. Check the intake time and the route.
warnings.unsupportedConcentrationUnit: The concentration unit is not supported, or a mass↔molar conversion is missing a molecular weight.
warnings.noTerminalHalfLife: The model reports no usable terminal half-life for this route, so extrapolating in time is not possible.
warnings.observationMatrixAssumed: The measured concentration is read as {{matrix}} — the model’s own matrix. No matrix conversion is applied to the observation, so a result from another matrix must be converted before it is entered.

drugMerge.title: Merge drugs
drugMerge.description: Fold two catalog entries for the same substance into one. The entry with a written monograph is kept; the other's data — parameters, source entries, analytical-method (rettstoks) memberships, metabolite and precursor links, and reference-atlas rows — is moved onto it, links to the removed page are updated, and the duplicate is deleted.
drugMerge.searchPlaceholder: Search by name, alias or CID…
drugMerge.conflictsHelp: Both entries hold a value for these. Choose which one the merged drug keeps.
drugMerge.blockersHelp: The merged drug would end up with a value the applicability system declares undefined. Resolve this on the drugs first (clear the value, lift the marker, or change the substance class), then merge.

blockerReason.marker_vs_value: one entry marks this parameter not-applicable while the other has a value or source entry for it
blockerReason.substance_class: the surviving substance class declares this parameter undefined, but there is a value or source entry for it

drugMerge.profileNoteHelp: Only the note text is chosen here — citations from both entries are always preserved on the surviving profile.
drugMerge.dataConflictsHelp: The two entries hold rows under the same identity key with different validated data (forensic method figures, cohort statistics, pKa measurements, or metabolic edges with independent evidence). A merge cannot pick between two independent measurements silently. Reconcile them on the drugs first — drop or correct one — then merge.
drugMerge.classMismatchHelp: The two entries disagree about what this substance IS — winner is "{{winner}}", loser is "{{loser}}". Substance class decides which parameters are defined at all (bioavailability and dose ranges are undefined for non-administered classes), so it cannot be silently adopted. Reconcile the classification on the drugs first, then merge.

errors.generic: The merge failed. Try again, and reload the page if it keeps failing.
errors.same_drug: Pick two different drugs to merge.
errors.not_found: One of the two drugs no longer exists — reload the page.
errors.substance_class_mismatch: The two entries disagree on substance class. Reconcile the classification on the drugs first, then merge.
errors.applicability_conflict: The merge would leave a value where the applicability system declares the parameter undefined. Resolve it on the drugs first, then merge.
errors.data_conflict: The merge would drop divergent validated data — two independently curated rows disagree on identity-key columns. Reconcile them on the drugs first, then merge.
errors.unresolved_conflicts: Some conflicts are unresolved. Re-run the preview and pick a side for each.
errors.stale_plan: The merge plan changed while it was being reviewed — a conflict value shifted, the loser monograph gained prose, or a new refusal appeared. Re-run the preview so the current picture is the one being approved.

winnerReason.byMonograph: "{{winnerName}}" (id {{winnerId}}) has a monograph and "{{loserName}}" (id {{loserId}}) does not, so it keeps its identity.
winnerReason.bothHaveMonograph: Both entries have a written monograph; defaulted to the more-used one. Confirm which should survive — the other monograph's prose will be discarded.
winnerReason.neitherHasMonograph: Neither entry has a written monograph; defaulted to the more-used entry. Confirm which should survive.

warnings.loserHasContent: The entry being removed ("{{loserName}}", id {{loserId}}) has a written monograph. Its prose will NOT be carried over — only structured data is merged. Copy anything worth keeping into the surviving monograph first.
warnings.seedFixtureReseed: The entry being removed has PubChem CID {{pubchemCid}}, which is still keyed in {{sources}}. The next seed run for any of these will recreate the duplicate — or silently attach the fixture's data to whichever surviving drug now claims that internal id. Prune or retarget every named entry before the next seed run, or the merge will silently reverse.

dataConflict.analyticalMethodFigures: both entries carry a membership in this method with different validated figures ({{what}}) — two forensic measurements, not one written twice
dataConflict.pmDistributions: two order-statistic transcriptions of the same source disagree — a merge cannot pick one without inventing a number, and JSONB concat of `printed` would let the loser silently overwrite significant-figure choices on any shared statistic
dataConflict.ionizationMeasurement: both entries record the same equilibrium but disagree on {{what}} — an admin-side merge cannot substitute one measurement for another (esp. for a curated row overwritten by a deep-research one)
dataConflict.metaboliteEvidence: both entries claim this metabolic edge and the loser row carries its own evidence (conversion fraction, activity, note, or citations) — dropping it would silently retire a distinct claim
dataConflict.metaboliteNameDifferentDrug: both entries have a {{what}} edge under the same name but the name resolves to different drugs (or the loser has resolved it and the winner still holds it as a free-text link). A name-only dedup would silently drop the loser's resolved id. Reconcile on the drugs first (change one label, or resolve the winner's link to match), then merge.
dataConflict.receptorMeasurement: both entries record this receptor mechanism but disagree on {{what}} — a silent pick would attach the loser's citation to the winner's number
dataConflict.enzymeStrength: both entries record this enzyme interaction but disagree on strength — a silent pick would substitute one rating for another
dataConflict.selfEdgeEvidence: this edge would become a self-edge on the surviving drug after the merge, but it carries real evidence (conversion fraction, activity, note, or citations). A silent delete would retire the claim — reconcile it on the drugs first (drop the edge or re-target its resolved drug)
dataConflict.monographProposals: the loser monograph has unfinished review-queue proposals. A merge would delete the page and drop the proposals with it. Settle or move them from the /review queue first, then merge.
dataConflict.fullReplacementProposals: the {{side}} has unfinished {{kind}} proposal(s) whose approval REPLACES the drug's whole {{kind}} list. A merge would leave the proposal authored against the pre-merge row set, so approving it later would wipe every row the merge just folded in or preserved. Settle it from the /review queue (approve, reject, or re-submit against the merged drug) first, then merge.
dataConflict.fullReplacementProposalsLateInsert: a {{kind}} proposal was submitted against the {{side}} while this merge was preparing to commit. Approving it after the merge would REPLACE the merged drug's whole {{kind}} list with a payload authored against the pre-merge row set. Settle it from the /review queue first, then merge again.
dataConflict.wikiNewLateInsert: a wiki_new proposal was submitted against the {{side}} while this merge was preparing to commit. Approval after the merge would publish either a second monograph on the survivor or a page for a drug that no longer exists. Settle it from the /review queue first, then merge again.
dataConflict.wikiNewOnLoserWithWinnerMonograph: the {{side}} has active new-monograph proposals but the survivor will already own a monograph after the merge. Retargeting or approving them would publish a second monograph on the survivor (wiki_pages has no drug_cid uniqueness). Settle the proposals from the /review queue — reject, or fold their content into the survivor as sections/facts — then merge.
dataConflict.multiMonograph: the {{side}} has more than one monograph page — a modern id-keyed page AND a legacy PubChem-CID-keyed page both resolve to it. On the loser the merge would delete only one and leave the other attached to a deleted drug; on the winner link rewrites and the fingerprint read would land on an arbitrary slug/page id and the survivor would remain ambiguously attached to more than one monograph. Delete or merge the extra page(s) first, then merge.
dataConflict.orphanedEntryProposal: a param_entry {{kind}} proposal targets a loser-side entry that would be dropped by the identical-row dedup at merge time — the retarget step only handles 'create' proposals, so approval would fail with param_entry_target_missing. Settle it from the /review queue (approve, reject, or move to the equivalent winner entry) first, then merge.
dataConflict.parameterEntryDivergentN: both entries have an identical observation for {{parameter}} but disagree on sample size (n={{winnerN}} vs n={{loserN}}). A normal insert would reject the duplicate; a merge cannot pick one n without silently changing the survivor's aggregate weight. Reconcile on the drugs first (merge the n values, drop one row, or file them under distinct citations), then merge.
dataConflict.parameterEntryDivergentComments: both entries have an identical observation for {{parameter}} but hold different curator comments (winner: "{{winnerComment}}"; loser: "{{loserComment}}"). Source entries stay additive across the fold, so a silent dedup would drop the loser's note. Reconcile on the drugs first (merge the comments, or file the observations under distinct citations), then merge.
dataConflict.parameterEntrySelfInteraction: source entry {{entryId}} records {{parameter}} with one of these drugs measured or dosed in the presence of the other — an interaction study that treats them as two different substances. Merging would turn it into a drug interacting with itself. Correct or remove that entry on the drugs first if they really are one substance, then merge.
dataConflict.parameterEntryThirdPartyDuplicate: source entries {{firstEntryId}} and {{secondEntryId}} record the same {{parameter}} observation for another drug, one naming each of these drugs as the drug given or coadministered. Once they are merged the two are one observation recorded twice, and it would be counted twice. Remove one of them on that drug first, then merge.
dataConflict.pendingEntrySelfInteraction: open proposal {{pendingEditId}} records a value with one of these drugs measured or dosed in the presence of the other. Merging would turn it into a drug interacting with itself. Settle it from the /review queue first, then merge.
dataConflict.parameterEntryDivergentObservationContex: both entries have an identical observation for {{parameter}} but disagree on study context — either stating different text, or one stating none while a quote is attached somewhere in the group (values seen: "{{winnerContext}}" / "{{loserContext}}"). Unlike a curator note, this is evidence a stored quote attests to — a silent dedup could keep one context at random or leave a quote attached to a context it was never checked against. Reconcile on the drugs first (merge the context, or file the observations under distinct citations), then merge.
dataConflict.parameterEntryDivergentQuotes: both entries have an identical observation for {{parameter}} and cite the same source, but quote different text from it (winner: "{{winnerQuote}}"; loser: "{{loserQuote}}"). One of them is reading the wrong sentence, which is exactly the error a stored quote exists to expose — a silent dedup would pick one at random and bury the disagreement. Check the source and keep the quote that states this value, then merge.
dataConflict.pendingParameterProposal: both entries have an open review-queue proposal for this parameter — merging would silently discard the loser's. Resolve one from the /review queue first, then merge.
dataConflict.revisionHistory: the loser monograph is empty now but has revisions with meaningful content in them (paragraph prose, images, headings, tables, lists or other structural nodes). `wiki_revisions` cascades on the page delete, so a merge would destroy editorial history that blanking the page did not. Move the content onto the survivor, or accept the loss deliberately by clearing the history first, then merge.
dataConflict.ambiguousSimulatorKey: the {{role}} saved-simulator key "{{key}}" names two substances — one drug carries it as its PubChem CID and another CID-less drug carries it as its internal id. Rewriting saved cases by that string would sweep up the other drug's cases too. Correct the CID collision on the drugs first, then merge.
dataConflict.parameterEntryAmbiguousOrigin: a loser observation for {{parameter}} states no study context and would be dropped as a duplicate, but its origin ("{{loserOrigin}}") is stronger than at least one of the {{winnerRowCount}} winner rows sharing this identity under different contexts — and which one it verifies cannot be determined without a context to match against. Dropping it silently would lose that provenance. Reconcile on the drugs first (add a context to the loser observation, or file it under a distinct citation), then merge.

citationMerge.title: Merge citations
citationMerge.description: Fold several citation rows that are really the same paper — for example the same article cited with slightly different spellings — into one. Everything attached to the removed rows (claims and parameter values citing them, paper reviews, stored PDFs, PDF upload requests and wiki references) moves to the one you keep, and the duplicates are deleted. This cannot be undone.

problems.title: This has to be put right before the case can be filed

problem.duplicate_specimen_id: Two specimens share the id {{id}}. Observations name a specimen by id, so one would be read against the other's matrix.
problem.quantified_without_value: Observation {{id}} is marked quantified but carries no value.
problem.quantified_without_unit: Observation {{id}} is marked quantified but carries no unit.
problem.negative_value: Observation {{id}} states a negative concentration. A measurement cannot be below zero.
problem.duplicate_observation_id: Two observations share the id {{id}}. An edit is applied by id, so correcting one would rewrite both.
problem.no_module: The case must name at least one substance module. The profile is framed around the module's assumed parent.
problem.duplicate_module: The case names the same substance module twice.
problem.dangling_specimen: Observation {{id}} names specimen {{specimenId}}, which the case does not carry. It would vanish from the profile with nothing saying so.
problem.exposure_range_backwards: The exposure window runs from {{earliest}} h to {{latest}} h, which is backwards.
problem.exposure_time_outside_range: The exposure is stated both at {{hours}} h and within the window {{earliest}}–{{latest}} h. The two do not say the same thing.
problem.time_origin_death_moved: The origin is the time of death, so death is at 0. The case states {{hours}} h.
problem.time_origin_first_specimen_untimed: The origin is the first specimen collection, but no specimen states a time. The specimen the origin refers to has to be at 0.
problem.time_origin_first_specimen_shifted: The earliest specimen is at {{hours}} h while the origin is the first specimen collection. Every hour in the case is shifted by that much.
problem.time_origin_no_exposure: The origin is a declared exposure, but the case declares none to measure from.
problem.time_origin_exposure_not_zero: The origin is a declared exposure, so the exposure it refers to has to be at 0. None of them is. A window places the intake but does not say where the axis begins.
problem.analyte_invalid: The analyte has no valid PubChem CID.
problem.limit_not_positive: The threshold must be greater than zero. No method has a reporting limit of zero.
problem.creatinine_not_positive: Creatinine must be greater than zero — it is the denominator of the creatinine normalisation.
problem.creatinine_reference_not_positive: The creatinine reference must be greater than zero.
problem.reported_as_invalid: The reported-as substance has no valid catalogue id.
problem.mass_basis_unweighable: Observation {{id}} is reported in a mass unit on a substance the catalogue cannot weigh (CID {{cid}}). The conversion to molar fails and the row becomes indeterminate.
problem.unreadable: The field {{path}} cannot be read under the current schema.
problem.time_origin_death_without_postmortem: The origin is the time of death, but the case is not marked postmortem. Its hours are measured from something the case says did not happen.
problem.death_instant_on_living_case: The case places the time of death on its axis but is not marked postmortem. The field is hidden for a living case, so the timestamp would stay there unseen.
problem.urine_data_on_other_matrix: Specimen {{id}} is not urine but carries urine data. Clear it, or set the matrix back to urine.
problem.exposure_amount_not_positive: A stated dose must be greater than zero.
problem.collection_duration_negative: A collection cannot last a negative time.
problem.postmortem_interval_negative: A postmortem interval cannot be negative.
problem.storage_duration_negative: A storage duration cannot be negative.
problem.duplicate_exposure_id: Two declared exposures share the id {{id}}. The rows are told apart by it, so one row's entry can end up on the other.

meaning.C: exploratory — read with the limitations below

dimensionWhy.completeness: a required input is missing or was filled from a conservative default.
dimensionWhy.primary-source-review: no named qualified reviewer has yet checked the decisive sources in full.
dimensionWhy.parameter-provenance: a value traces only to a study or table, not to a reproducible extraction.
dimensionWhy.population-applicability: the source population differs materially from the one selected, and the direction of the difference is unknown.
dimensionWhy.matrix-route-match: the curve is shown in a matrix reached by an unvalidated blood:plasma conversion.
dimensionWhy.validation-status: the model has not been checked against independent observed concentrations.
dimensionWhy.uncertainty-semantics: the band combines uncertainty sources, so its probability meaning is not established.
dimensionWhy.unresolved-contradictions: sources disagree materially and no branch has been selected.

cautiousDefault.bioavailability: Cautious default: the catalog holds no bioavailability for this route, so the curve assumes the whole dose is absorbed (100%). Concentrations are therefore likely too high, and a dose worked back from a concentration is likely too low.
cautiousDefault.generic: Cautious default: the catalog holds no value for {{parameter}}, so the curve uses a labelled default.

modelGrade.simplifiedStructure: Simplified model: the sources state “{{declared}}”, but this curve is computed as “{{runs}}”, because the catalog does not yet hold the parameters the stated model needs.
modelGrade.noBandReported: This run reports a single value, not an interval: the model declares fixed parameter values, so the uncertainty is not quantified.
